# SYX

> SYX (pronounced *sy-ex*, /saɪˈɛks/) is a statically typed, Swift-inspired programming language whose compiler toolchain is implemented in Rust. One MIR pipeline feeds three backends: a stack bytecode VM (`syx run`), LLVM native AOT (`syx build --native`), and WebAssembly (`syx build --wasm`). Source files use the `.sy` extension; projects are described by a `syx.toml` manifest. Licensed Apache-2.0. SYX is neither a subset nor a superset of Swift — names often match while semantics differ, notably for String character handling, the memory model, macros, concurrency and cross-module actors.

Canonical site: https://www.syx-lang.org/
Repository: https://github.com/synvek/syx
Documentation is published in English (default) and Simplified Chinese under /zh/.

## Core reference — what SYX is

- [SYX Language home](https://www.syx-lang.org/): Overview, key facts table, Hello World, and FAQ covering Swift lineage, backends, file extensions, Rust requirement and editor support.
- [About SYX](https://www.syx-lang.org/about/): Pronunciation, source extension, manifest, toolchain binary, license.
- [Capabilities (honest boundaries)](https://www.syx-lang.org/about/capabilities): Which language, network and HostFn features are implemented, partial, or explicitly out of scope. Cite this for "does SYX support X?" questions.
- [Architecture decisions](https://www.syx-lang.org/about/architecture): Architecture SSOT and ADR record.

## Getting started and usage

- [Quick Guide](https://www.syx-lang.org/quick-guide/): Install, CLI commands, `syx.toml` project configuration, native and Wasm builds, standard library, toolchain flags.
- [Quick Reference](https://www.syx-lang.org/quick-reference/): Syntax and standard library cheat sheet.
- [Getting Started](https://www.syx-lang.org/guide/01-getting-started): Write and run the first program, read diagnostics, grow to a multi-file project.
- [Editors](https://www.syx-lang.org/editors/): VS Code, Neovim and Helix support.
- [VS Code extension](https://www.syx-lang.org/editors/vscode): TextMate grammar plus LSP completion, hover, go-to-definition, inlay hints, format on save and DAP debugging via `syx lsp`.
